identity.name: GCP BigQuery Foreign-Project Exfil via Impersonated Service Account — Cortex ABIOC (T1537 / T1078.004)
identity.summary: A caller mints short-lived tokens for a privileged BigQuery service account it has never impersonated (iamcredentials GenerateAccessToken), then exports query results to a project outside the org — the GCP audit-log shape of foreign-project exfiltration. An Analytics impersonation alert and a foreign-project-exfil ABIOC fire on the deviations; a correlation stitches them on the caller principal.
identity.description: This card exercises Cortex XSIAM's cloud Analytics Behavioral IOCs (ABIOCs) on the GCP Cloud Audit Log data source (both the Data Access and Admin Activity streams normalise to the cloud_audit_logs dataset). The technique is the credential-abuse-to-exfiltration chain Unit 42 documents against GCP: an over-permissioned caller (a compromised user or workload identity holding roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator) impersonates a privileged BigQuery service account by calling iamcredentials.googleapis.com GenerateAccessToken, then uses the borrowed identity to run a BigQuery job whose destination — an extract to a bucket, a copy table, or a query results table — lands in a project outside the organization boundary. No single API call is a known-bad IOC: GenerateAccessToken and BigQuery InsertJob are legitimate calls made constantly in a healthy GCP estate, which is exactly why a hand-authored BIOC keyed on a method name would drown in false positives. The two detections that ARE the named XSIAM cloud-audit alerts — 'GCP service account impersonation attempt' (an Analytics alert) and 'BigQuery table or query results exfiltrated to a foreign project' (an auto-tuned ABIOC) — fire on the DEVIATION from learned behavior and anchor it to a causality chain. The impersonation Analytics alert fires when a caller principal impersonates a service account it (and its peer group) has no learned history of impersonating, anchored to the iamcredentials GenerateAccessToken call. The exfil ABIOC fires when a BigQuery job writes results to a foreign destination project that diverges from the caller's learned set of destination projects, anchored to the borrowed-identity session. Two validation XQL queries confirm the emitted GCP audit records landed in cloud_audit_logs; a correlation rule fuses the impersonation Analytics alert and the foreign-project-exfil ABIOC on the shared caller principal into a single foreign-project-exfil incident the DC presents as proof that Cortex behavioral analytics caught a data-theft chain built entirely from legitimate cloud API calls. The scenario drives the shape-true logs into an operator-supplied collector via the cloud_audit_emitter analytics streamer (provider=gcp) — no real GCP tenant is touched and no real data leaves.

actors.name: Cloud intruders abusing stolen or over-permissioned GCP identities for cross-project data theft

campaigns: GCP credential abuse — impersonate a privileged service account then exfiltrate BigQuery data to an attacker-controlled foreign project (2023-2026)

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-CDR-022 — GCP BigQuery foreign-project exfil via impersonated service account (cloud_audit_emitter provider=gcp) for Cortex ABIOC validation

prerequisites.description: Cortex XSIAM / Cortex Cloud CDR ingesting the GCP Cloud Audit Logs (Data Access + Admin Activity) into cloud_audit_logs so per-identity impersonation and BigQuery job activity is profiled.
A baseline window has elapsed so Cortex learned each service account's normal impersonation callers and its normal set of BigQuery destination projects.
An operator-supplied HTTP collector (XSIAM Broker VM / log forwarder) is wired into XSIAM as a GCP audit source and reachable from the jumpbox.

payload.code:
# No real GCP mutation and no real data movement. Drive the cloud_audit_emitter
# analytics streamer (provider=gcp) to POST shape-true GCP Cloud Audit Log
# records into the operator collector: first a service-account impersonation
# burst (iamcredentials GenerateAccessToken), then a BigQuery job whose results
# are exported to a foreign project.
set -euo pipefail
: "${COLLECTOR_URL:=https://collector.cortexsim-canary.invalid/cloud/events}"
: "${COLLECTOR_HOST:=collector.cortexsim-canary.invalid}"
cat > /tmp/cdr-022-gcp-impersonation.yml <<YML
campaign_id: CMP-CDR-022
name: "CDR-022 — GCP service-account impersonation"
authorized_by: "domain-consultant@paloaltonetworks.com"
simulation_authorized: true
target_allowlist:
  - "${COLLECTOR_HOST}"
dry_run: false
steps:
  - step_id: step-01
    plugin: cloud_audit_emitter
    params:
      collector_url: "${COLLECTOR_URL}"
      provider: gcp
      event_pattern: service_account_impersonation
      iterations: 1
YML
cat > /tmp/cdr-022-gcp-bq-exfil.yml <<YML
campaign_id: CMP-CDR-022
name: "CDR-022 — GCP BigQuery foreign-project exfil"
authorized_by: "domain-consultant@paloaltonetworks.com"
simulation_authorized: true
target_allowlist:
  - "${COLLECTOR_HOST}"
dry_run: false
steps:
  - step_id: step-01
    plugin: cloud_audit_emitter
    params:
      collector_url: "${COLLECTOR_URL}"
      provider: gcp
      event_pattern: bigquery_exfiltration
      iterations: 1
YML
python3 -m scripts.eal_simulator.cli run /tmp/cdr-022-gcp-impersonation.yml --live
python3 -m scripts.eal_simulator.cli run /tmp/cdr-022-gcp-bq-exfil.yml --live

abiocs.name: GCP Service Account Impersonation Attempt
abiocs.description: A caller principal mints short-lived credentials for a service account by calling iamcredentials.googleapis.com GenerateAccessToken, impersonating a service account that neither this caller nor its learned peer group has a history of impersonating. Every call is a legitimate IAM operation; this Cortex Analytics alert fires on the new caller-to-service-account impersonation edge — the deviation from the learned impersonation graph — anchored to the iamcredentials call rather than to any known-bad method name. The cloud_audit_emitter GCP builder emits only GenerateAccessToken for this preset (the impersonated principal is carried in the top-level target_service_account shape hint), so the logic keys on that single fully-qualified methodName rather than a leaf-name list.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter protoPayload.serviceName = "iamcredentials.googleapis.com"
| filter protoPayload.methodName = "google.iam.credentials.v1.IAMCredentials.GenerateAccessToken"
| comp count() as impersonation_calls by protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail, target_service_account, protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp
| filter impersonation_calls >= 1
| sort desc impersonation_calls
| fields protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail, target_service_account, protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp, impersonation_calls
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned per-caller and per-peer-group service-account impersonation graph -> a caller principal (protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail) issues an iamcredentials GenerateAccessToken for a target_service_account new to its learned impersonation set, anchored to the impersonation call and its protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp.

abiocs.name: BigQuery Table or Query Results Exfiltrated to a Foreign Project
abiocs.description: A BigQuery job (query-results write / extract) run by a caller writes its output to a destination project that diverges from the account's learned set of destination projects — the shape of data exfiltration to a project outside the organization boundary. The individual InsertJob call is legitimate; the ABIOC fires on the foreign-destination-project deviation from the identity's learned BigQuery behavior. The cloud_audit_emitter GCP builder tags the exfil record with the foreign_project=true shape hint and the foreign destination_project_id, so the logic keys on that emitted deviation flag and destination project rather than an unemitted resource-vs-destination inequality.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter protoPayload.serviceName = "bigquery.googleapis.com"
| filter protoPayload.methodName = "google.cloud.bigquery.v2.JobService.InsertJob"
| filter foreign_project = true
| comp count() as foreign_project_jobs by protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail, destination_project_id
| filter foreign_project_jobs >= 1
| sort desc foreign_project_jobs
| fields protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail, destination_project_id, foreign_project_jobs
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned per-caller BigQuery destination-project set -> a BigQuery InsertJob writes results to a foreign project (foreign_project=true, destination_project_id outside the learned set), anchored to the caller principal (protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail) that submitted the job.

xql_queries.name: CDR-022 Service Account Impersonation Events Landed in Cloud Audit Log
xql_queries.query:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter protoPayload.serviceName = "iamcredentials.googleapis.com"
| filter protoPayload.methodName = "google.iam.credentials.v1.IAMCredentials.GenerateAccessToken"
| comp count() as impersonation_events by protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail, target_service_account
| filter impersonation_events >= 1
| fields protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail, target_service_account, impersonation_events

xql_queries.name: CDR-022 BigQuery Foreign-Project Export Landed in Cloud Audit Log
xql_queries.query:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter protoPayload.serviceName = "bigquery.googleapis.com"
| filter protoPayload.methodName = "google.cloud.bigquery.v2.JobService.InsertJob"
| filter foreign_project = true
| comp count() as foreign_project_jobs by protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail, destination_project_id
| filter foreign_project_jobs >= 1
| fields protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail, destination_project_id, foreign_project_jobs

correlation_rules.name: Foreign-Project BigQuery Exfil via Impersonated Service Account — ABIOC Causality Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: ANALYTICS(GCP Service Account Impersonation Attempt) AND ABIOC(BigQuery Table or Query Results Exfiltrated to a Foreign Project) on the same caller principal (protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail) within the run window — fuses the borrowed-identity mint (target_service_account) and the foreign-project BigQuery export (destination_project_id, foreign_project=true) into one cross-project data-exfil incident anchored to the shared caller principal (caller identity -> impersonated service account -> BigQuery job to a foreign project).

use_cases.name: GCP BigQuery Foreign-Project Exfil via Impersonated Service Account — Cortex ABIOC Validation
use_cases.description: Cortex's auto-tuned Analytics Behavioral IOCs learn each service account's impersonation callers and BigQuery destination-project set, and detect a credential-abuse-to-exfiltration chain anchored to the impersonation causality chain — where every underlying GCP API call is legitimate and no static rule was written for it.

test_cases.objective: The impersonation and foreign-project-exfil ABIOCs both fire on the injected GCP audit records and the correlation stitches them into one incident.
preconditions: Cortex XSIAM / Cortex Cloud CDR ingesting the GCP Cloud Audit Logs into cloud_audit_logs.
Baseline window elapsed so per-SA impersonation callers and BigQuery destination projects are learned.
Operator collector reachable and wired into XSIAM as a GCP audit source.
steps: Let the per-service-account baseline window elapse.
Emit a service-account impersonation burst (iamcredentials GenerateAccessToken) via cloud_audit_emitter provider=gcp.
Emit a BigQuery job whose results export to a foreign project via cloud_audit_emitter provider=gcp.
Observe both ABIOCs fire and CR-CDR-0022 raise one foreign-project-exfil incident.
success_criteria: ABIOC `GCP Service Account Impersonation Attempt` fires.
ABIOC `BigQuery Table or Query Results Exfiltrated to a Foreign Project` fires.
Correlation CR-CDR-0022 raises one stitched foreign-project-exfil incident anchored to the impersonated service account.

preventive_controls: Scope roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator narrowly and prefer per-resource IAM conditions so a compromised identity cannot impersonate privileged BigQuery service accounts.
Enforce a VPC Service Controls perimeter around BigQuery so query results and extracts cannot be written to projects outside the organization boundary.
Constrain BigQuery job destinations with organization policy (resource-location and allowed-projects constraints) and disable cross-project copy/extract for privileged datasets.
detection_engineering: Let Cortex auto-tune ABIOCs against the learned per-caller service-account impersonation graph rather than hand-authoring static rules on GenerateAccessToken.
Alert on a BigQuery job whose destination project diverges from the service account's learned destination-project set.
Stitch the impersonation and foreign-project-export ABIOCs on the shared impersonated service-account principal into one exfil incident.
